description: Core error taxonomy and Result-style types for the kernel
steps: Define a base AppError class plus specific subclasses (ValidationError, ConfigError, PluginLoadError, CapabilityDeniedError)
Write unit tests asserting each error carries a stable machine-readable code and safe (non-leaking) public message
Verify errors serialize to a JSON shape suitable for API error envelopes without including stack traces by default

description: Layered configuration system (defaults -> env -> operator overrides) validated with zod
steps: Implement a config loader that merges default config, process.env, and an optional local override file
Define a zod schema for core config (port, log level, node env)
Write unit tests: missing required var fails fast with a clear error; valid config loads correctly; overrides take precedence in the right order

description: Structured logger with automatic secret redaction
steps: Wrap pino to produce structured JSON logs with request/plugin context fields
Implement a redaction list (password, secret, token, apikey, authorization) applied before any log line is emitted
Write unit tests proving a log call containing a secret-like field never appears in the emitted output

description: Plugin manifest schema (plugin.json) and zod validator
steps: Define the manifest shape: id, version (semver), depends_on (semver ranges), capabilities.provides, capabilities.requires, entry point
Implement a zod schema and a validateManifest() function returning typed errors for every violation
Write unit tests covering valid manifests and at least 5 invalid variants (bad semver, missing id, duplicate capability, malformed capability grammar, unknown field)

description: Plugin directory discovery and scanning
steps: Implement a scanner that walks src/plugins/*, reads each plugin.json, and returns raw manifest + directory path pairs
Skip and log (do not crash on) directories missing a plugin.json
Write unit tests against a temp fixture directory tree with valid, missing-manifest, and malformed-manifest plugins

description: Dependency graph resolution: topological sort, semver range checks, cycle detection
steps: Build a dependency graph from discovered manifests using depends_on semver ranges
Implement topological sort producing a deterministic load order
Detect and reject circular dependencies with a clear error naming the cycle
Write unit tests: linear chain, diamond dependency, missing dependency, version range mismatch, and a 3-node cycle

description: Capability broker: declare, grant, and revoke inter-plugin capabilities
steps: Implement a broker where a plugin can only obtain a capability handle it declared in capabilities.requires and that is registered by a provider
Ensure there is no ambient/global way to reach another plugin's internals outside the broker
Write unit tests: granted capability is usable, undeclared capability request is denied, revoked capability stops working immediately

description: Plugin loader: instantiate plugins in dependency order and run lifecycle hooks
steps: Implement loader that, given the sorted graph, calls onInstall/onEnable in order, wiring each plugin's granted capabilities via the broker
Support onDisable/onUninstall in reverse dependency order
Write unit tests with fixture plugins asserting hook call order matches the dependency graph

description: Typed event bus for cross-plugin publish/subscribe
steps: Implement an event bus with typed event names and payloads (no `any`), supporting multiple subscribers per event
Ensure a throwing subscriber cannot prevent other subscribers of the same event from running
Write unit tests: multiple subscribers, unsubscribe, and isolation from a throwing handler

description: Error isolation: a failing plugin cannot crash the kernel or unrelated plugins
steps: Wrap plugin load and lifecycle hook execution in try/catch that logs and marks only that plugin as failed
Ensure a failed plugin's failure does not prevent independent plugins (no depends_on relationship) from loading
Write unit tests: a plugin that throws in onEnable results in only that plugin (and its dependents) being marked failed

description: In-memory audit trail sink for capability grants and permission checks
steps: Define an AuditSink interface (record(event)) and a default in-memory implementation with a query API
Wire the capability broker to record every grant/deny decision to the audit sink
Write unit tests asserting grants, denials, and revocations all produce audit entries with actor/target/outcome/timestamp

description: Kernel bootstrap: wire config, logger, registry, loader, event bus, and audit sink together in src/server/index.ts
steps: Replace the placeholder bootstrap with real kernel construction: load config, build logger, discover plugins, resolve dependencies, load in order
Ensure a fatal config or manifest error produces a clear, single, non-stack-trace startup error message and a non-zero exit code
Run npm run dev and confirm the process boots cleanly with zero plugins present, then again after later plugins exist

description: Kernel introspection API: report loaded plugins, their capabilities, and load status
steps: Implement a programmatic kernel.introspect() returning plugin id, version, status (loaded/failed/disabled), and granted capabilities
Write a small CLI script (or npm script) that prints this report in human-readable form
Write unit tests asserting the report reflects load failures and disabled plugins accurately

description: Kernel unit/integration test suite covering registry, loader, broker, and error isolation together
steps: Write an integration test that loads a fixture set of 4-5 plugins with a realistic dependency graph end-to-end through the real bootstrap path
Include a case with one intentionally broken plugin and assert the rest still load
Run npm test and confirm the whole kernel suite is green

description: Written plugin conventions spec: naming rules, capability grammar (resource:action), forbidden cross-plugin imports
steps: Write docs/plugin-conventions.md documenting the manifest shape, capability naming grammar, directory layout, and import rules
Cross-check the doc against the actual zod schema so they cannot silently drift (a shared constant or generated snippet)
Have at least one existing kernel test assert the documented capability grammar regex matches the validator's actual regex

description: Runtime plugin enable/disable without a full process restart
steps: Implement kernel.disablePlugin(id) / enablePlugin(id) that run the appropriate lifecycle hooks and update introspection status
Ensure disabling a plugin that others depend on is rejected with a clear error listing the dependents
Write unit tests: disable/re-enable a leaf plugin succeeds; disabling a depended-upon plugin is rejected

description: database-mysql plugin manifest declaring db:query, db:transaction, db:migrate capabilities
steps: Create src/plugins/database-mysql/plugin.json following the conventions from feature 15
Validate the manifest passes the kernel's manifest validator
Write a unit test asserting the plugin is discoverable and its manifest is valid

description: MySQL connection pool with validated config and optional TLS
steps: Implement pool construction from DB_* env vars via the zod config schema, using mysql2's promise pool
Fail fast at startup with a clear error if required DB config is missing or malformed
Write unit tests for config validation; write an integration test that connects to the docker-compose MySQL instance

description: Migration runner: versioned, checksum-verified, up/down, tracked in a migrations table
steps: Implement a migrations table (id, name, checksum, applied_at) and a runner that applies pending migrations in order
Detect and reject a modified already-applied migration file via checksum mismatch
Implement `npm run migrate` and `npm run migrate:down`; write an integration test applying and rolling back a sample migration

description: db:query capability implemented via kysely, parameterized only
steps: Wire a kysely Kysely<Database> instance over the mysql2 pool and expose a typed db:query capability
Ensure there is no code path that accepts raw interpolated SQL strings from capability consumers
Write an integration test performing a parameterized SELECT/INSERT and asserting SQL injection payloads are treated as literal data

description: db:transaction capability with commit/rollback semantics
steps: Expose a transaction(fn) capability that commits on success and rolls back on any thrown error
Write an integration test: a transaction with a failing statement midway leaves no partial writes

description: Per-plugin schema/table namespace enforcement
steps: Define and document a table naming convention (e.g. `<plugin_id>_<table>`) and enforce it in the migration runner
Reject a migration that creates a table violating another plugin's namespace
Write a unit test asserting a misnamed table migration is rejected with a clear error

description: Connection resilience: retry with backoff and pool exhaustion handling
steps: Implement exponential backoff retry for transient connection errors on startup and mid-session
Return a clear, safe error (not a raw driver exception) to capability consumers when the pool is exhausted
Write a test simulating a temporarily unreachable DB and asserting the retry/backoff behavior

description: Database health check integrated into kernel introspection
steps: Expose a health-check function on the db:query capability that runs a trivial SELECT 1
Wire it into the kernel introspection report from feature 13 as a per-plugin health field
Write a test asserting introspection reports 'unhealthy' when the DB is unreachable

description: Seed data / fixtures mechanism for local development
steps: Implement a seed runner separate from migrations (idempotent, dev-only) that other plugins can register seed functions with
Wire it into init.sh behind an explicit flag so production runs never seed automatically
Write a test asserting seeds are idempotent (running twice does not duplicate rows)

description: Slow query logging and basic query performance metrics
steps: Instrument the db:query capability to log queries exceeding a configurable duration threshold, with parameters redacted
Track basic counters (query count, error count, average duration) queryable via kernel introspection
Write a test asserting a deliberately slow query is logged and counted

description: Integration test suite for database-mysql against dockerized MySQL
steps: Cover migrations up/down, db:query CRUD, db:transaction rollback, and namespace enforcement in one suite that runs against docker-compose MySQL
Wire this suite to run in CI (depends on the CI pipeline feature) with a MySQL service container
Run npm test locally with docker-compose mysql up and confirm all pass

description: Backup and restore helper scripts
steps: Write a mysqldump-based backup script and a matching restore script, parameterized by env config
Document usage in docs/backup-restore.md
Write a test (can be a shell-invoking integration test) that backs up and restores a small dataset and asserts row-for-row equality

description: Persist the kernel audit trail into MySQL once the database plugin is available
steps: Add an audit_log migration under the database-mysql namespace convention
Implement a MySQL-backed AuditSink and swap it in during bootstrap once database-mysql has loaded, falling back to in-memory if the DB plugin is disabled
Write an integration test asserting audit events recorded during a session are queryable from the database after restart

description: Expose connection pool metrics (active/idle/queued) via kernel introspection
steps: Add pool metrics collection to the connection pool wrapper
Surface them through the health-check/introspection integration from feature 24
Write a test asserting metrics update correctly under concurrent queries

description: rbac plugin manifest declaring rbac:check and rbac:manage capabilities
steps: Create src/plugins/rbac/plugin.json following conventions from feature 15
Validate the manifest against the kernel's validator
Write a unit test asserting the plugin is discoverable and valid

description: Core RBAC data model: roles, permissions (resource:action grammar), role-permission and user-role associations
steps: Design in-memory types/interfaces for Role, Permission, and the association tables ahead of persistence
Implement a permission-string parser/validator enforcing the resource:action grammar from feature 15
Write unit tests for the parser covering valid and invalid permission strings

description: Policy evaluation engine: can(user, action, resource)
steps: Implement can() resolving a user's roles to permissions and evaluating against the requested action/resource, deny-by-default
Support wildcard permissions (e.g. wiki:* ) with explicit, documented precedence rules
Write unit tests covering allow, deny-by-default, wildcard match, and conflicting-role scenarios

description: Persistent storage for roles, permissions, and assignments via database-mysql
steps: Add roles/permissions/role_permissions/user_roles migrations under the rbac_ table namespace
Reimplement the data access layer to read/write through the db:query capability instead of in-memory structures
Write an integration test: create a role, assign a permission, assign to a user, restart, and confirm state persisted

description: Policy decision caching with invalidation on role/permission change
steps: Add an in-process cache for can() results keyed by (user, action, resource) with a short TTL
Invalidate affected cache entries immediately on any role/permission/assignment mutation
Write a test proving a permission revoked mid-session is denied on the very next check, not after the TTL

description: Role and permission management operations (create/update/delete role, assign/revoke permission and role)
steps: Implement the management operations as a typed programmatic API ahead of any HTTP surface
Enforce that only callers already holding rbac:manage may invoke them (self-referential check)
Write unit tests for each operation including failure paths (duplicate role name, assigning a nonexistent permission)

description: Seed default roles and permissions (admin, editor, viewer)
steps: Register a seed (via the seed mechanism from feature 25) creating admin/editor/viewer roles with a sensible starter permission set
Ensure the seed is idempotent
Write a test asserting seeding twice does not create duplicate roles

description: Audit logging of every access-check decision
steps: Wire can() to record allow/deny decisions to the kernel audit trail with user, action, resource, and outcome
Ensure high-frequency checks do not overwhelm the audit sink (batch or sample if needed, documented tradeoff)
Write a test asserting a denied check produces a queryable audit entry

description: Expose rbac:check as a consumable capability for other plugins
steps: Register the can() function as the rbac:check capability through the broker
Write a fixture consumer plugin that requests rbac:check and uses it, proving the cross-plugin contract works
Write an integration test for the fixture consumer

description: Bootstrap-admin safety mechanism to prevent permanent lockout
steps: On first run with zero users holding the admin role, provision a bootstrap admin account/token and log it prominently once
Ensure the bootstrap path is disabled automatically once at least one admin exists
Write a test simulating first-run vs. already-provisioned states

description: RBAC unit and integration test suite (policy engine, caching, persistence, audit)
steps: Assemble a suite exercising the full stack: seeded roles, can() checks, cache invalidation, and audit trail together
Run against dockerized MySQL
Run npm test and confirm all pass

description: Permission grammar validator rejects malformed resource:action strings at every entry point
steps: Apply the parser from feature 32 at every boundary that accepts a permission string (seed data, management API, config)
Write unit tests for malformed inputs at each entry point (not just the parser itself)

description: Role hierarchy / inheritance support
steps: Extend the data model to allow a role to inherit permissions from parent role(s), with cycle detection
Update can() to resolve inherited permissions
Write unit tests for a 2-level hierarchy and a rejected cyclic hierarchy

description: RBAC admin HTTP routes (list/create/update roles, assign/revoke permissions)
steps: Register routes through the api-gateway http:route capability, protected by rbac:check requiring rbac:manage
Validate request/response payloads with JSON schema
Write an integration test hitting the routes as an admin (allowed) and as a viewer (403 denied)

description: html-renderer plugin manifest declaring the render:template capability
steps: Create src/plugins/html-renderer/plugin.json following conventions
Validate the manifest
Write a unit test asserting the plugin is discoverable and valid

description: Template parser/compiler: variables, conditionals, loops
steps: Implement a small template language (mustache/handlebars-inspired) supporting {{var}}, {{#if}}, {{#each}}
Compile templates to reusable render functions rather than re-parsing on every render
Write unit tests for variable interpolation, nested conditionals, and loops over arrays/objects

description: Context-aware auto-escaping (HTML body, attribute, URL, JS contexts)
steps: Detect the syntactic context of each interpolation site at compile time and apply the matching escaper
Default every interpolation to escaped output with no way to accidentally opt out
Write unit tests with adversarial strings (<script>, " onmouseover=, javascript: URLs) for each context, asserting safe output

description: Layout system (base layout plus content blocks)
steps: Implement layout templates that define named blocks a child template fills in
Support nested layouts (a layout extending another layout)
Write unit tests rendering a child template through a 2-level layout chain

description: Partials/components (reusable, parameterized template fragments)
steps: Implement a partial-inclusion syntax that accepts parameters and renders in an isolated scope
Guard against infinite partial recursion with a max-depth error
Write unit tests for parameterized partials and the recursion guard

description: Explicit raw/unescaped output helper, audited
steps: Add an intentionally verbose {{{raw expr}}} or similar syntax for the rare unescaped case
Every use of the raw helper logs an audit entry (plugin id, template, expression) via the kernel audit trail
Write a test asserting raw output is unescaped and produces an audit entry

description: Theme/asset pipeline (static CSS/JS serving with cache headers)
steps: Implement a static asset registration API plugins can use to publish CSS/JS/images under a namespaced path
Set appropriate Cache-Control/ETag headers on served assets
Write a test asserting a registered asset is served with correct headers and content

description: Expose render:template as a consumable capability
steps: Register the compile/render functions as the render:template capability through the broker
Write a fixture consumer plugin proving the cross-plugin render contract works end-to-end
Write an integration test for the fixture consumer

description: Compiled template caching with dev-mode invalidation on file change
steps: Cache compiled render functions keyed by template path + mtime/hash
In development, detect source file changes and recompile; in production, cache is immutable per process lifetime
Write a test asserting a changed template is picked up in dev mode and cached (not recompiled) in production mode

description: XSS regression test suite across all escaping contexts
steps: Build a table-driven test of known XSS payloads rendered through HTML/attribute/URL/JS contexts and the raw helper
Assert every non-raw context neutralizes every payload
Wire this suite into CI as a required check

description: Safe error page templates (404/500) that never leak stack traces in production
steps: Create default 404 and 500 templates rendered via the layout system
Ensure the 500 template only shows internal detail when NODE_ENV=development
Write a test asserting production mode hides error detail and development mode shows it

description: Unit test suite for html-renderer (parser, layouts, partials, caching)
steps: Assemble tests covering the parser, layout nesting, partials, and the template cache together
Run npm test and confirm all pass

description: api-gateway plugin manifest providing http:route and consuming rbac:check/render:template optionally
steps: Create src/plugins/api-gateway/plugin.json following conventions
Validate the manifest
Write a unit test asserting the plugin is discoverable and valid

description: Fastify instance owned by api-gateway, mounted into kernel bootstrap
steps: Move Fastify construction out of the placeholder bootstrap and into the api-gateway plugin's onEnable hook
Kernel bootstrap starts listening only after all plugins have loaded successfully
Update the smoke test to go through the real bootstrap path and confirm /health still responds

description: http:route capability: typed route registration API for other plugins
steps: Expose a registerRoute({method, path, schema, handler}) capability wrapping Fastify's route API
Enforce that every registered route declares a request/response JSON schema
Write an integration test where a fixture plugin registers a route and it is reachable over HTTP

description: Request validation and a consistent 4xx error envelope
steps: Wire Fastify's schema validation to reject invalid requests with a uniform JSON error shape ({code, message, details})
Write an integration test posting an invalid payload and asserting the exact error envelope shape

description: Centralized error handler with a consistent envelope and no stack-trace leaks in production
steps: Implement a Fastify error handler that maps thrown AppError subclasses (feature 1) to HTTP status codes and safe messages
Ensure unexpected errors return a generic 500 body in production but full detail in development logs
Write a test asserting a thrown internal error never appears in the HTTP response body in production mode

description: API versioning convention (/api/v1/...)
steps: Extend registerRoute to prefix routes with a version segment, defaulting to v1
Document the versioning/deprecation policy in docs/api-versioning.md
Write a test asserting a registered route is reachable at the versioned path

description: Session/cookie handling with secure defaults
steps: Wire @fastify/cookie with HttpOnly, Secure (config-driven), and SameSite=Lax defaults
Implement a signed session identifier issuance/verification helper
Write a test asserting a session cookie is issued with the correct flags and a tampered cookie is rejected

description: CSRF protection for state-changing routes
steps: Implement a double-submit-cookie or synchronizer-token CSRF scheme applied to POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE routes by default
Provide an explicit, audited opt-out for routes that are safe by construction (e.g. pure JSON APIs with strict CORS + no cookies)
Write a test asserting a state-changing request without a valid CSRF token is rejected

description: RBAC middleware integration: per-route required permission
steps: Extend registerRoute with an optional requiredPermission field checked via rbac:check before the handler runs
Return 401 for unauthenticated and 403 for authenticated-but-unauthorized, without leaking which one more than necessary
Write an integration test for allowed, unauthenticated, and forbidden cases on a protected fixture route

description: Configurable rate limiting (global and per-route)
steps: Wire @fastify/rate-limit with global defaults from env config and support for stricter per-route overrides
Return a standard 429 with Retry-After on limit exceeded
Write a test that exceeds the limit and asserts a 429 response

description: Security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.) via helmet
steps: Wire @fastify/helmet with a sensible default policy, configurable per-deployment
Write a test asserting the expected security headers are present on responses

description: Configurable CORS allow-list
steps: Wire @fastify/cors driven by the CORS_ORIGIN env config, denying by default for unlisted origins
Write a test asserting an allowed origin gets CORS headers and a disallowed origin does not

description: Pagination and filtering helpers for list endpoints
steps: Implement shared query-param parsing (page/limit/sort/filter) with validation and sane upper bounds
Provide a helper that turns parsed params into kysely query modifiers
Write a test for a fixture list route covering default, custom page size, and out-of-range page requests

description: OpenAPI documentation auto-generated from registered routes
steps: Derive an OpenAPI 3 document from each route's JSON schema and expose it at /api/v1/openapi.json
Add a minimal Swagger UI (or equivalent) route for human browsing
Write a test asserting the generated document includes a route registered by a fixture plugin

description: Request size limits and timeout configuration
steps: Configure Fastify body size limits and request timeouts from env config
Write a test asserting an oversized payload is rejected before reaching the handler

description: api-gateway integration test suite (routing, validation, RBAC gating, rate limiting, CSRF, error envelope)
steps: Assemble an end-to-end suite exercising the gateway as a whole against fixture routes
Run npm test and confirm all pass

description: plugin-builder plugin manifest
steps: Create src/plugins/plugin-builder/plugin.json following conventions
Validate the manifest
Write a unit test asserting the plugin is discoverable and valid

description: Publish the plugin.json JSON Schema for external/programmatic reuse
steps: Export the kernel's zod manifest schema as a standalone JSON Schema file under this plugin
Keep it generated from the single source of truth (feature 4) rather than hand-duplicated
Write a test asserting the exported schema validates the same fixtures the kernel validator does

description: create-plugin generator: scaffolds manifest, lifecycle stubs, src/, tests/
steps: Implement a generator function taking a plugin id and description, emitting a valid plugin directory from templates
Ensure generated output passes the kernel's manifest validator unmodified
Write a test that generates a plugin into a temp dir and validates every emitted file

description: CLI entry point wiring `npm run create-plugin`
steps: Implement the CLI (src/plugins/plugin-builder/src/cli.ts) with prompts/flags for id, description, and capabilities
Wire it to package.json's create-plugin script
Write a test invoking the CLI programmatically (non-interactive flags) and asserting correct output

description: Static conventions linter for plugin directories
steps: Implement a linter checking naming, capability declaration completeness, and forbidden cross-plugin internal imports
Run it against every shipped plugin as part of the test suite so drift is caught automatically
Write unit tests with a passing fixture and 3 failing fixtures (bad naming, undeclared capability use, forbidden import)

description: AI-agent-facing plugin authoring guide
steps: Write docs/ai-plugin-authoring.md: an unambiguous, example-rich spec of the manifest, capability grammar, and directory conventions aimed at an AI coding agent as the reader
Include a worked example referencing the real rbac and database-mysql plugins as canonical patterns
Have a teammate/agent unfamiliar with the codebase attempt to follow only this doc to generate a trivial plugin, and record any ambiguity found as a doc fix

description: Reference hello-world plugin generated and proven to load in the real kernel
steps: Use the generator from feature 75 to create a hello-world plugin committed to src/plugins/
Confirm it loads successfully at kernel bootstrap and appears in kernel introspection
Write an integration test asserting hello-world loads without modification after regeneration

description: Programmatic generator API (usable by another plugin or an AI agent, not just the CLI)
steps: Expose the generator as an importable function with a typed options object, independent of any CLI/stdin interaction
Write a test invoking the programmatic API directly, bypassing the CLI

description: Capability cross-check warnings in the generator/linter
steps: Extend the linter to warn when a plugin declares capabilities.requires for a capability no loaded plugin provides
Write a test asserting the warning fires for an intentionally mismatched fixture

description: Capability index doc generator (which plugin provides/consumes what)
steps: Implement a script that scans all plugin manifests and emits a Markdown table of provided/required capabilities
Wire it to run in CI and fail if the checked-in doc is stale (regenerate and diff)
Write a test asserting the generated table includes every shipped plugin's declared capabilities

description: Generator output validity test suite
steps: Assert generated plugin output passes both the manifest validator and the conventions linter automatically as part of npm test
Cover generation with the minimal option set and with a fuller option set (capabilities, description)

description: Plugin manifest version bump helper
steps: Implement a small utility that safely bumps a plugin's semver version in plugin.json and validates the result
Write a test asserting an invalid target version is rejected and a valid one updates the file correctly

description: wiki plugin manifest (depends on rbac:check, db:query, render:template, http:route)
steps: Create src/plugins/wiki/plugin.json following conventions, declaring all four required capabilities
Validate the manifest
Write a unit test asserting the plugin is discoverable and valid

description: Database schema/migrations: pages, revisions, namespaces
steps: Add wiki_pages, wiki_revisions, wiki_namespaces migrations under the wiki_ table namespace
Include appropriate indexes (namespace+slug uniqueness, revision lookup by page)
Write an integration test applying the migrations and asserting constraints (unique slug per namespace) are enforced

description: Page CRUD via the db:query capability
steps: Implement create/read/update/delete for wiki pages entirely through db:query, no direct SQL client usage
Enforce slug format validation and namespace existence on create
Write integration tests for each CRUD operation including not-found and duplicate-slug error paths

description: Markdown-to-HTML rendering via html-renderer's render:template
steps: Implement a safe Markdown parser (no raw HTML passthrough by default) producing an AST or HTML string fed into render:template as data, not as a raw string
Ensure the auto-escaping from feature 47 still applies to any user-controlled text inside the rendered output
Write a test rendering a page containing an XSS-style payload in Markdown and asserting it is neutralized

description: Revision history: every edit creates a revision row
steps: On every page update, snapshot the previous content into wiki_revisions before applying the change
Implement an endpoint/function to list revisions for a page in reverse-chronological order
Write a test asserting 3 sequential edits produce 3 retrievable revisions in the correct order

description: Diff view between two revisions
steps: Implement a line-based diff between any two revisions of the same page
Render the diff safely through html-renderer (no raw HTML injection from diffed content)
Write a test asserting additions/deletions are correctly identified for a known before/after pair

description: Page tree / navigation sidebar reflecting namespace hierarchy
steps: Implement a query building a nested tree structure from wiki_namespaces and page slugs
Write a test asserting a 3-level namespace hierarchy produces the correct nested structure

description: Full-text search across pages
steps: Add a MySQL FULLTEXT index on page title/content and implement a search function using it, with a LIKE-based fallback path documented for non-FULLTEXT-capable configurations
Rank results by relevance and return snippets with the matched term highlighted (safely escaped)
Write a test asserting a search term matches the expected pages and irrelevant pages are excluded

description: RBAC integration: read/write/admin permissions per page or namespace
steps: Define the wiki: permission grammar (wiki:read, wiki:write, wiki:admin, optionally namespaced) and apply rbac:check on every mutating and restricted-read operation
Default to viewer-readable/editor-writable unless a namespace overrides it
Write integration tests for allowed and denied access at each permission level

description: Wiki HTTP routes via api-gateway (list/get/create/update/delete/search/history/diff)
steps: Register all wiki routes through the http:route capability with JSON-schema validation and the appropriate requiredPermission per route
Apply the API versioning convention from feature 62
Write an integration test suite hitting every route over real HTTP against a test server instance

description: Wiki home page and navigation UI rendered via html-renderer layouts
steps: Build the home page and page-view templates using the layout/partial system from html-renderer
Wire the navigation sidebar from feature 91 into the shared layout
Write a test rendering the home page and asserting key navigation elements are present

description: Page edit form UI with CSRF-protected submission
steps: Build create/edit page templates with a form posting through the CSRF-protected route from feature 64
Show validation errors returned by the API inline in the form
Write a test asserting a submission without a valid CSRF token is rejected end-to-end through the real UI flow

description: Attachments/file upload support for wiki pages
steps: Implement size-limited, content-type-validated file upload tied to a page, stored outside the webroot with randomized storage names
Serve attachments through an authorization-checked route (respecting the page's permissions), never directly from a static directory
Write a test asserting an oversized or disallowed-type upload is rejected, and a valid upload is retrievable only by an authorized user

description: Wiki-level audit log surfaced via the kernel audit trail
steps: Record create/update/delete/permission-denied events for wiki pages to the kernel audit trail with actor and page identity
Provide a simple admin view/query listing recent wiki audit entries
Write a test asserting an edit produces a queryable audit entry with the correct actor

description: Wiki seed content (starter Home page and platform documentation)
steps: Register a seed creating a Home page and a few docs pages describing the platform itself (dogfooding spec.md content)
Ensure the seed is idempotent
Write a test asserting seeding twice does not duplicate the Home page

description: End-to-end wiki test suite (create/edit/view/search/permission-denied flows)
steps: Assemble a suite driving the real HTTP API (and, where practical, the rendered HTML) through a full page lifecycle including a permission-denied case
Run npm test and confirm all pass

description: Wiki rendered-page caching with invalidation on edit
steps: Cache rendered HTML for a page keyed by page id + revision id
Invalidate (or simply let the key change) immediately on any edit
Write a test asserting a stale cached render is never served after an edit

description: Accessibility pass on wiki HTML templates
steps: Review wiki templates for semantic HTML, form label associations, and keyboard navigability
Fix identified issues (heading order, alt text on any images, focus states)
Write a lightweight automated check (e.g. axe-core against rendered HTML) as part of the test suite

description: CI pipeline: lint, typecheck, build, unit tests on push/PR
steps: Add a GitHub Actions workflow running npm ci, lint, build, and test on every push and pull request
Fail the workflow on any lint, type, or test error
Push a trivial branch/PR (or simulate locally with act, if available) and confirm the workflow definition is syntactically valid

description: Dependency vulnerability scanning in CI
steps: Add an `npm audit --audit-level=high` (or equivalent) step to the CI workflow
Document the remediation process for a flagged vulnerability in docs/security.md
Confirm the step fails the build on a high/critical finding by testing against a known-vulnerable fixture package.json in a scratch branch

description: Pre-commit hooks for lint and format on staged files
steps: Wire husky + lint-staged to run eslint --fix and prettier on staged files before commit
Document setup in README (one-time `npm install` sets up the hook)
Confirm a deliberately malformatted staged file gets auto-fixed on commit
